annotationRationale: Double counting team-subset incidences determines the required team count. Prime-exponent bounds characterize divisibility of the product of five consecutive integers, and simultaneous congruences count the admissible participant totals without duplication. The combination formula supports the subset calculations.
sourceMethod: Followed the official incidence count, prime-power divisibility tests, and Chinese remainder theorem count. Simplified the averages through binomial ratios and expanded the residue tests and the sufficiency of an integer team count.

review.mathCheck: Incidence counting gives \(M_k=T\binom{k}{5}/\binom{n}{5}\), hence \(T=\binom{n}{5}/84\). Integrality is sufficient because this many distinct teams can be chosen. Independently checking prime exponents gives respectively 5, 7 and 8 allowed residues modulo 7, 9 and 16. CRT therefore gives 280 classes modulo 1008. Removing 1 through 4 and adding 2017 yields \(560-4+1=557\), choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: An originally worded, faithful adaptation of MAA Q25, pages 12-13: incidence counting, prime-power divisibility and CRT. The candidate additionally explains the residue cases and sufficiency of the team count.
review.annotationCheck: The method is reconstructible at AMC 12 level. Multiplicities, positivity, distinct-team availability and both interval endpoints are handled correctly.
